statement.p: A density function is given by f(x)=\frac{1}{k!t^k}x^{k-1}e^{-x/t}\text{,} where x>0 and k,t>1 are constants. Find the mode of f(x)\text{.}

solution.p: The constant factor \frac{1}{k!t^k} is positive, so it does not affect where the maximum occurs. Differentiate the part depending on x\text{:}
Since x^{k-2}e^{-x/t} is positive for x>0\text{,} the critical point occurs when
The function increases before this point and decreases after it, so the mode is x=t(k-1)\text{.}
